rationale: The plan correctly identifies that a 1-vs-1 design supports no dispersion estimate and therefore no valid test, and it explicitly withholds all p-values and FDR claims while naming the replicated design (n>=3/group) that would be required — this is the central requirement and it is met cleanly. QC (library sizes, blind VST distances, explicit statement that reproducibility cannot be assessed) is appropriate for two samples, the filter (>=10 counts in >=1 sample, tied to smallest group size) is minimal and justified, and normalization is median-of-ratios inside DESeq2 with an explicit prohibition on pre-scaling and an explicit control reference level. Two weaknesses: apeglm shrinkage is invoked on a design where the dispersion and coefficient standard errors it depends on cannot be estimated, so the 'shrunken' log2FC is not well defined; and the GO-ORA step, though carefully universe-anchored, size-windowed and caveated, is built on an arbitrary fold-change magnitude screen from a non-inferential comparison of two libraries — enrichment is not warranted here and would have been better omitted. The final report is thorough on versions, thresholds, gene counts and the design caveat.
